operations.description: API Endpoint to get all the candidates. This endpoint retrieves comprehensive information on all domain candidates for the job positions. operations.description: API Endpoint to create or update an applicant (and his application) for the specified job position. This endpoint facilitates the creation of a new applicant for the specified job position. The job position must be published. The request body should include applicant's full name (first name and last name), an email, an address, a phone number, a brief description and his/her resume. If you intend to update the information for the current applicant, you have to use the same email address as it is associated with the applicant's existing record. When an applicant successfully submits their application for a job position, two emails are automatically generated and sent. The first email is sent to the creator of the job position, notifying them that a new applicant has been added to the pool of candidates for the position they created. The second email is dispatched to the applicant, serving as a confirmation of their job application submission. Filenames within the system must not start with any illegal character or symbol (e.g. @ (at sign), $ (dollar sign), % (percent), & (ampersand)) and should maintain a reasonable length, ensuring they do not exceed 250 characters. Request body: Name Type Required Description Values first_name string true Maximum character limit: 191 characters. last_name string true Maximum character limit: 191 characters. email string true Maximum character limit: 191 characters. Valid email format and structure. phone string true Maximum character limit: 191 characters. address string true Maximum character limit: 191 characters. description string true Maximum character limit: 30,000 characters. resume file true File. Valid Formats (docx,doc,odt,pdf). The document must not surpass 30MB. answers array or json string false Answers to this job position's ATS custom questions. Send either (a) an array of answer objects or (b) a JSON string of that array. If the job position has required active ATS custom questions, this field becomes required. Each item must include question_id . Depending on the question type, send either text (free-text questions) or answer_id (single-choice / multiple-choice questions).

operations.name: Create ATS job position custom question
operations.description: Create ATS job position custom question Creates an ATS application custom question for job position applications. Defines the question text, whether it is mandatory, the question type, and when the type is single-choice or multiple-choice a list of answer choices. Requires permission to create ATS application custom questions. Use Get ATS custom question type values (GET https://pubapi.talenthr.io/v1/job-positions/custom-questions/values ) for custom_question_type_id values under data.custom_question_types . Request body: Name Type Required Description Values body string yes Question text shown to applicants. Maximum 1000 characters. e.g. List three relevant certifications. is_required boolean yes Whether applicants must answer this question. JSON booleans only. e.g. false custom_question_type_id integer yes Question type id from Get ATS custom question type values ( data.custom_question_types ). e.g. 1 answers array conditional Required when the type is single-choice or multiple-choice. Each object requires body (choice label). Do not include id on create. May be sent as a JSON array or a JSON string that decodes to an array. Omit for text, long text, link, and date types. e.g. [{"body":"Yes"},{"body":"No"}] There are no path parameters.

operations.name: Get ATS job position custom question
operations.description: This endpoint returns one ATS job position custom question by numeric id. The data object includes nested custom_question_type and custom_answers . Requires permission to view that custom question.

operations.name: Update ATS job position custom question
operations.description: This endpoint updates the editable fields on an existing ATS job position custom question. The request body uses the same keys as Create ATS job position custom question. When custom_question_type_id changes to or from choice types, the server reapplies answers according to internal rules (a type change may clear prior choices unless you supply a valid answers payload for the new type). When the question remains a single-choice or multiple-choice question, the answers array is the authoritative set of choices. Each existing choice you intend to keep or update must be sent with its numeric id (from custom_answers ) and with body ; choices not listed with their id are deleted. New choices are sent as body with id omitted or with id set to JSON null . The response data shape matches Get ATS job position custom question. Requires permission to update that question. Request body Name Type Required Description Values body string yes Question text shown to applicants. Maximum 1000 characters. e.g. Updated question text is_required boolean yes Whether applicants must answer this question. JSON booleans only. e.g. true custom_question_type_id integer yes Question type id from Get ATS custom question type values ( data.custom_question_types ). Changing the type may clear or require a new answers payload when moving to or from single-choice or multiple-choice. e.g. 1 answers array conditional Required when the type is single-choice or multiple-choice. Each object requires body . Include id for existing choices to retain or update them; omit id or send JSON null for new choices. Choices not listed with their id are removed. May be sent as a JSON array or a JSON string that decodes to an array. Omit for text, long text, link, and date types. e.g. [{"id":10,"body":"Yes"},{"body":"No"}]

Requires permission to create asset custom fields. Use Get type and permission values (GET https://pubapi.talenthr.io/v1/custom-fields-values ) for type ids and permission actions/conditions. Use List user roles (GET https://pubapi.talenthr.io/v1/user-roles ) for user_role_id values in each permissions row. Request body: Name Type Required Description Values name string yes Display name for the field definition. e.g. Warranty end date custom_field_type_id integer yes Field type id from Get type and permission values ( data.type_values ). Use an entry where is_visible is true; the group type is not accepted on create. e.g. 1 asset_type_slug string or null no Limits the definition to one asset product type when set. Omit the property, send JSON null , or use inventory or membership only. e.g. inventory permissions array yes Access rules by user role for asset field view and edit. Send as a JSON array (a JSON string is also accepted). Each object: user_role_id (from List user roles ), action ( view or edit ), and condition (string or array of strings). Allowed values are under data.permission_values in Get type and permission values . Do not send resource or value in the request body. e.g. [{"user_role_id":5,"action":"view","condition":["all"]},{"user_role_id":5,"action":"edit","condition":["manager"]}] values array conditional Required when the field type is single-choice or multiple-choice. Each object requires text (option label). e.g. [{"text":"Option A"},{"text":"Option B"}] There are no path parameters.

Send as a JSON array (a JSON string is also accepted). Each object: user_role_id (from List user roles ), action ( view or edit ), and condition (string or array of strings). operations.name: Update an asset status
operations.description: API Endpoint to change the status of the specified asset. This endpoint allows for the modification of an asset's status, applicable to both inventory and membership assets, with each type having its distinct set of statuses. For membership assets, there are only two possible statuses: Available : Indicates the asset is ready and accessible for use. Retired : Signifies that the asset is no longer in service or use. Inventory assets, on the other hand, have a broader range of five possible statuses: Available : The asset is not currently being used and is ready for deployment. In Use : Indicates the asset is actively being utilized. In Service : The asset is undergoing maintenance or repairs. Broken : The asset is damaged and not in working condition. Retired : Similar to the membership asset, this status means the asset is no longer in service. For inventory assets with an assigned user, the transition to the "In Use" status is specifically relevant when the asset is moving from a "Broken" or "In Service" status. It is important to note that once an inventory asset is marked as "Retired," any association with an assigned user is removed, effectively preventing any further transition to the "In Use" status. Request body: Name Type Required Description Values asset_status_slug enum true The slug of the asset status. If the asset type is "membership", the available actions are limited to "available" and "retired". However, if the type is "inventory", the available options expand to include [available, in-use, in-service, broken, retired]. For an inventory asset with an assigned user, transitioning to the "in-use" status is applicable primarily when the current status is "broken" or "in-service". When the status is "retired", the assigned user is no longer associated, thus preventing a transition to the "in-use" status. in-use, available, in-service, broken, retired

operations.name: Delete an employee
operations.description: API Endpoint to delete the specified employee. This API endpoint facilitates the deletion of a specified employee from the system based on the provided employee ID. Upon invoking this endpoint, the system permanently removes the employee's record, along with all associated information and data stored within the system. It triggers a cascading effect that removes all associated records and data related to that employee. This includes various items such as job records, employment status, performance, review, assets,benefits information, personal documents, task assignments and any other information tied directly to the employee's profile. Before deleting the employee, the system checks if any other employees report to him/her directly. If there are, these subordinate employees are automatically reassigned to a new manager. Typically, the new manager is the supervisor of the deleted employee. This ensures that there is no disruption in the workflow and that the responsibilities of the deleted employee are seamlessly redistributed within the organization. Warning: If the employee being deleted is the head of the company, meaning they have no manager above them in the organizational hierarchy, the deletion cannot proceed. Note: Once an employee is deleted, their email address can be used on your domain again.

operations.name: Terminate an employee
operations.description: API Endpoint to terminate the employment of an employee. This API endpoint demonstrates the process of employee terminations within the HR system by incorporating the effective date of termination and the reason for termination. Users can remain active and utilize the system normally until the final termination date is specified. Upon the termination process, the system automatically assigns offboarding tasks to relevant users, ensuring a seamless transition for the terminated employee (employees are being notified also via email). If the termination date matches the current date, the user is instantly terminated, preventing further access to the system. When an employee is terminated, the system initiates several automatic procedures to ensure a smooth transition and maintain organizational integrity. Upon the employee's termination, employees who are under his/her supervision are reassigned to the manager of the terminated employee. Concurrently, any incomplete task assignments of the terminated employee are transferred to this manager as well. Furthermore, the system automatically deletes any job records, compensation records, manager records, or employment status records that are dated after the termination. Additionally, any time off requests(rejected or remain unanswered) from the terminated employee will be removed. Finally, if the terminated employee is part of a hiring team for a job position, he/she will be removed from the hiring team as part of the termination process. Note: The information of the terminated user remains within the system after the termination. Request body: Name Type Required Description Values effective_date date true The date that an employee will be terminated. The effective date must be formatted as 'YYYY-MM-DD'. e.g. 2024-02-01 termination_reason string false The reason for the employee's dismissal. Maximum character limit: 4000 characters. e.g. poor quality of work termination_type string false The type of termination. If omitted, it defaults to termination . Available values: termination , resignation regrettable_status string false Indicates whether the termination is regrettable. If the termination is not regrettable, omit this parameter or set it to null . Available value: regrettable

operations.description: API Endpoint to book a time off request. This endpoint facilitates the booking of a time-off request for the specified employee. A time off request is an entity that describes the decision making process for approving time off. It can be used for various reasons such as vacation, personal matters, bereavement or illness. The request body includes the start and end dates for the time-off request, the type of time-off requested, the preapproved attribute indicating whether the request will be automatically approved or requires manager approval, the amount option providing a detailed analysis of each day's duration (e.g., full-day as 1, half-day as 0.5, etc), and can include hours in the per-day breakdown when hour-based amounts apply, optional notes accompanying the request, and an optional file attachment for supporting documents (sent as the multipart attachment part when used; see the request body table for size and type rules). For future-hire employees, the time-off request cannot have a start date before their hire date. For terminated employees, the time-off request must come before the termination date. Note: The start_date and end_date must fall within one year from the current date. When the "book time off" request is successfully submitted and preapproved is false or the part is omitted, an email is automatically dispatched to the employee's manager, requesting approval or rejection of the time off request. If the manager is currently off work and thus unable to respond, an email notification is sent to the employee, informing them that their manager is presently unavailable to address the request. Request body (form-data): Name Type Required Description Values start_date string yes Interval start date in YYYY-MM-DD format. Must be on or after the employee hire date when applicable, must not follow the termination date when applicable, must fall within one year of the current date, and must fall within a valid time off cycle. e.g. 2026-04-01 end_date string yes Interval end date in YYYY-MM-DD format (inclusive). Must be on or after start_date ; same hire, termination, one-year, and cycle rules as start_date . e.g. 2026-04-05 timeoff_type_id integer yes Time off type id. Must reference a non-deleted, enabled time off type. e.g. 3 preapproved boolean no When true , uses the pre-approve permission path when the caller is allowed and the request may be auto-approved when permitted; when omitted or false , uses the standard create permission and normal approval flow. In multipart, send as the text true or false . e.g. false amount_options string no Optional multipart text field whose value is JSON encoding per-day amounts for every date from start_date through end_date (inclusive). Each date value is either a day fraction ( 1 , 0.5 , 0 , …; minimum 0.001 when non-zero) or an object with amount_days and/or amount_hours —not both styles on the same date. Use 0 for non-working days and holidays where required. e.g. {"2024-01-10":1,"2024-01-11":0.5} note string no Optional note. Maximum 255 characters. e.g. Doctor appointment attachment file no Optional supporting document (multipart part named attachment ). Allowed types: docx, doc, odt, odp, ods, xls, xlsx, ppt, pptx, pdf, png, jpg, jpeg, svg, csv, gif, webp, tsv, txt. Maximum size 30000 KB. file (optional)

operations.description: API Endpoint to create an employee. This API endpoint facilitates the creation of an employee within the system. When creating an employee, it's necessary to provide essential personal information such as first name, last name, and email address. Additionally, the endpoint requires details regarding the employee's hire date, employment status, and manager. When we are adding a new employee, we should avoid creating loops or circles in the organization hierarchy. If the is_existing parameter is set to true the onboarding process is bypassed. Otherwise, if it's set to false, the employee is considered a new hire, and the system initiates the onboarding process for the newly hired employee. In cases where no manager is specified, the employee becomes the head of the company hierarchy. You can choose to disable the initial system invite. In case you want to provide some additional information on onboarding new hires at the organization, you should fill in the hire packet object with the necessary information. This allow you to send an a email to the hiring employee containing detailed instructions for their first day of work. After the successful creation of a newly hired employee's profile, an email is dispatched to the new hire containing essential information required for registering with the domain. This includes details such as login credentials, and any other relevant information to facilitate their smooth integration into the company's systems. Additionally, emails are sent to existing employees who are assigned the responsibility of conducting the onboarding tasks for the new employee. Request body: Name Type Required Description Values first_name string true Maximum character limit: 191 characters. e.g. John last_name string true Maximum character limit: 191 characters. e.g. Doe email string true It has to be valid email format and structure. The email has to be unique. e.g. john.doe@example.com hire_date date true The hire date must be formatted as 'YYYY-MM-DD'. e.g. 2024-01-10 reports_to_employee_id integer true The employee Id that will be the manager of the current employee. If the reports_to_employee_id is 'null' then the current employee will be the head of the company. - employment_status object true Object with properties: employment_status_id (integer). e.g. {"employment_status_id": 1} job_record object false Object with properties: job_title_id (integer,nullable), location_id (integer,nullable), division_id (integer,nullable), department_id (integer,nullable). All the variables must be present. e.g. {"job_title_id": 1, "location_id": 12, "division_id":null, "department_id":20} compensation_record object false Object with properties: pay_rate (integer), pay_rate_period (enum,nullable) [hour, day, week, month, quarter, year], pay_schedule (enum,nullable) [once-per-month, twice-per-month, every-other-week], overtime_status (enum,nullable) [exempt, non-exempt] e.g. {"pay_rate": 1000, "pay_rate_period": "day", "pay_schedule":"once-per-month", "overtime_status":null} prevent_email boolean false Opt for 'true', if you don't want to send an invitation email to the hiring employee, else 'false'. - is_existing boolean false Opt for 'false' if the employee is a new hire and you want to run the Automatic Onboarding process, else 'true'. - hire_packet object false Info for the new hire.Object with properties: who_id (integer, id of employees), address (string), when_time (date-time), instructions (string) e.g. {"who-id":1, "address": "Random Str 123A", "when_time":"2024-03-10 17:00", "instructions": "These are some instructions..."}

operations.description: Create employee custom field Creates a tenant-defined employee custom field with a display name, field type, role-based permissions, and—when the type is single-choice or multiple-choice—a list of option labels. Use Get type and permission values ( GET custom-fields-values ) for allowed type ids ( data.type_values ; do not use the group type on create) and permission actions/conditions. Use List user roles ( GET user-roles ) for user_role_id values in each permissions row. Request body: Name Type Required Description Values name string yes Display name for the field. Maximum 255 characters; must be unique per server rules. e.g. Certification tier custom_field_type_id integer yes Field type id from Get type and permission values ( data.type_values ). Use an entry where is_visible is true; the group type is not accepted on create. The type cannot be changed after creation. e.g. 4 permissions array yes Access rules by user role. Each object: user_role_id (from List user roles ), action , and condition (string or array of strings). Allowed action and condition values are listed under data.permission_values in Get type and permission values . e.g. [{"user_role_id":3,"action":"view","condition":["all"]},{"user_role_id":3,"action":"edit","condition":["manager"]}] values array conditional Required when the field type is single-choice or multiple-choice. Requires permission to update the custom field. Use Get type and permission values and List user roles for the same reference data as create. Request body: Name Type Required Description Values name string yes Display name for the field. Maximum 255 characters; must satisfy uniqueness rules. e.g. Certification tier (updated) custom_field_type_id integer yes Must equal the field’s existing type id (the API rejects type changes). Compare with data.type_values from Get type and permission values . e.g. 4 permissions array yes Access rules by user role. Each object: user_role_id , action , and condition . See data.permission_values in Get type and permission values . e.g. [{"user_role_id":3,"action":"view","condition":["all"]},{"user_role_id":3,"action":"edit","condition":["manager"]}] values array conditional Required when the field type is single-choice or multiple-choice. When provided, must be on or after today plus notify_before days. e.g. 2027-06-01 recipients array yes Who receives expiration reminders. Send as a JSON array (a JSON string is also accepted). At most three objects. Each object must include either id (employee id) or email , not both. operations.description: API Endpoint to set compensation band ranges. This endpoint replaces the tenant’s compensation band definitions used by compensation reports. Compensation bands partition annual compensation into contiguous ranges; each band uses a lower bound ( from ) and an optional upper bound ( to ) in the tenant’s compensation currency units. Requires permission to set compensation reports (not merely view). Every band except the last must include non-null from and to ; from must be strictly less than to . The last band may set to to null for an open upper bound; when to is present on the last band, from must be strictly less than to . Each from and to may be a JSON number or a numeric string (integer or decimal). On success, the response includes the persisted bands under data.ranges . Request body: Name Type Required Description Values compensation_ranges array or string yes Ordered list of compensation bands for the tenant. Send as a JSON array (canonical) or as a JSON string that decodes to the same array structure. Each element is an object with from and optional to . Every band except the last must include non-null from and to ; from must be strictly less than to . The last band may set to to null for an open upper bound; when to is present on the last band, from must be strictly less than to . Each from and to may be a JSON number or a numeric string (integer or decimal). e.g. [{"from":0,"to":50000},{"from":50000,"to":120000},{"from":120000,"to":null}]

operations.description: Create a survey Creates a new survey for the tenant. The survey starts on the specified start date, runs for the specified duration, and—if a recurrence is provided—repeats at that interval. The survey can target all employees or a defined audience, and responses can be anonymous. Requires permission to create a survey and a subscription that includes the Surveys feature. Request body: Name Type Required Description Values title string yes Survey title. Max 255 characters. e.g. Q2 engagement draft description string no Longer survey description. Max 5000 characters. e.g. Internal draft before publishing. survey_questions_description string no Intro text shown above questions when published. Max 5000 characters. e.g. Please answer all questions. survey_status string yes Target status slug. Active non-archived status from survey_statuses (see survey reference / defaults). e.g. draft start_date string (date) yes Tenant calendar date for scheduling. Domain date format: YYYY-MM-DD . e.g. 2026-04-01 duration string yes Cycle length. Must be one of: 3 days , 5 days , 15 days , 1 month . e.g. 15 days recurrence string or null no Repeat pattern. One of: 1 year , 6 months , 3 months , 1 month , or null for a one-off survey. e.g. null is_anonymous boolean no Whether responses are anonymous. e.g. false required_for_all boolean conditional When true , the survey targets all employees. When false , send survey_required_for with scoped audiences. e.g. false survey_required_for object conditional Required when required_for_all is false . Object must include exactly these keys: division , department , location , job_title , emp_state (employment status custom field ids), employee ; each value is an array of integer ids. At least one array must be non-empty; ids must exist in the tenant. e.g. {"division":[],"department":[],"location":[],"job_title":[],"emp_state":[],"employee":[15]} survey_questions array yes Template questions for the survey. Required; must be a non-empty array. Each element: body (string, required, max 1000), is_required (boolean), survey_question_type_id (integer from survey defaults), order (distinct positive integer). For single-choice and multiple-choice types, include an answers array of objects shaped as {"body":"..."} . e.g. [{"body":"How satisfied are you with team communication?","is_required":true,"survey_question_type_id":1,"order":1,"answers":[{"body":"Very satisfied"},{"body":"Somewhat satisfied"}]}] Use Get survey defaults for allowed statuses, durations, recurrence labels, and question type ids.       "order": "<integer>", // (Required) Distinct positive integers. Example: 1
      "answers": [ // Required for single/multiple choice; omit for plain text. Include answer id to update an existing option; omit id or null → new answer; any existing answer not listed here by id is deleted.
        { "id": "<integer>", "body": "<string>" }, // Existing answer id optional; omit or null → new answer row
        { "body": "<string>" } // Example: Somewhat satisfied
      ]
    }
  ] // Full example: [{"id":901,"body":"How satisfied are you?","is_required":true,"survey_question_type_id":1,"order":1,"answers":[{"id":1001,"body":"Very satisfied"},{"body":"Somewhat"}]}]
}
operations.description: Update a survey Updates an existing survey’s details, schedule, audience, anonymity settings, and questions. Not allowed while the survey is active and a cycle is currently open (HTTP 403). Requires permission to update this survey and a subscription that includes the Surveys feature. Request body: Name Type Required Description Values title string yes Survey title. Max 255 characters. e.g. Q2 engagement draft (revised) description string no Longer survey description. Max 5000 characters. e.g. Updated copy before the next publish. survey_questions_description string no Intro text shown above questions for respondents. Max 5000 characters. e.g. Please answer honestly; responses are aggregated by team. survey_status string yes Target status slug. Must be an active non-archived value from survey_statuses (see Get survey defaults ). e.g. draft start_date string (date) yes Schedule anchor. Domain date format: YYYY-MM-DD . e.g. 2026-04-01 duration string yes Cycle length. Must be one of: 3 days , 5 days , 15 days , 1 month . e.g. 15 days recurrence string or null conditional Repeat pattern. Allowed strings or null per product defaults; you cannot set null to clear recurrence if recurrence was already set on this survey. e.g. 3 months is_anonymous boolean no Whether responses are anonymous. e.g. false required_for_all boolean conditional When true , the survey targets all employees. When false , send survey_required_for with scoped audiences. e.g. false survey_required_for object conditional Required when required_for_all is false . Object must include exactly these keys: division , department , location , job_title , emp_state (employment status custom field ids), employee ; each value is an array of integer ids. At least one array must be non-empty; ids must exist in the tenant. e.g. {"division":[],"department":[],"location":[],"job_title":[],"emp_state":[],"employee":[15]} survey_questions array yes Full replacement list of template questions for this survey. Required; must be a non-empty array. For each question, include id to update an existing row (use ids from Get survey ); omit id or use null to create a new question; any existing question not listed here by its id is removed. Each element: body (string, required, max 1000), is_required (boolean), survey_question_type_id (integer), order (distinct positive integer). For single-choice and multiple-choice types, include an answers array; for each answer, include id to update an existing option, or omit id / use null to add a new one; any existing answer not listed by id is removed. e.g. [{"id":901,"body":"How satisfied are you?","is_required":true,"survey_question_type_id":1,"order":1,"answers":[{"id":1001,"body":"Very satisfied"},{"body":"Somewhat"}]}] Use Get survey defaults for allowed statuses, durations, recurrence labels, and question type ids.

operations.description: API Endpoint to create a new date range for blocked time off. This endpoint facilitates the creation of a new time off blocked period. This lets you block one or more date ranges from any type of time-off request. The request body should include the start date and end date of the blocked period, the time-off types affected by this period, whether the blocked period is currently active, and optionally the employee scope ( required_for_all / timeoff_blocked_date_required_for ). Note: If the timeoff_type attribute has an empty array, it indicates that the time off blocked period will be applicable for all time off types. Note: If required_for_all is true (or omitted on create), the blocked period applies to all employees. If required_for_all is false , you must provide timeoff_blocked_date_required_for with all keys present and at least one non-empty ID list. Request body: Name Type Required Description Values start_date date true The start date of blocked time off. The start date must be formatted as 'YYYY-MM-DD'. This date must be from today forth and before the last day of the next year. e.g. 2024-03-01 end_date date true The end date of blocked time off. The end date must be formatted as 'YYYY-MM-DD'. This date must be after start date and from the next year's last day and before. e.g. 2024-03-10 is_active boolean true Choose 'true' to activate the blocked period for time off, and 'false' to deactivate it. - timeoff_type array true Array of time off type Ids. This must be present and in case this attribute is empty, it applies to all time off types. e.g. [1,2,3,4] required_for_all boolean false When true, applies to all employees. When false, timeoff_blocked_date_required_for is required. Defaults to true on create if omitted. e.g. true timeoff_blocked_date_required_for object conditional Required when required_for_all is false. Grouped map with keys: location, division, department, job_title, emp_state, employee (each an array of IDs). At least one array must be non-empty. emp_state persists as employment_status . e.g. {"division":[58],"department":[],"location":[],"job_title":[28],"emp_state":[5],"employee":[131]}

Must be strictly before the current local time, after started_at , and within twenty-four hours of started_at . e.g. 2026-05-04 11:30:00 time_tracking_tag_id integer or null no Tag for the entry. Must be an id from time tracking tags assigned to this employee, or null or omitted when no tag applies. e.g. 12 Path parameters are documented under Params.

Requires permission to edit time tracking entries for that employee. The interval must not overlap other entries and cannot exceed twenty-four hours. query.description: (string) Optional. Allowed when not using a custom date range. Accepted values: today, yesterday, week, month. When period, start_date, and end_date are all omitted, the API applies today for validation. Other single-token values fail validation (HTTP 422).

query.name: start_date
query.description: (string) Optional. Start of a custom range in YYYY-MM-DD format. Used with end_date instead of period.

query.name: end_date
query.description: (string) Optional. End of a custom range in YYYY-MM-DD format; must be on or after start_date. Together with start_date must not span more than 36 months.

query.name: working_now
query.description: (boolean) Optional. Must be a boolean when present (for example true or false in query parsing). When evaluated as truthy, narrows results to the “working now” scope and omits company-wide aggregate keys such as available_tags and working_now_employee_ids from the response.

query.name: search
query.description: (string) Optional. Free-text filter applied to name, entry timestamp, location, division, department, and tag fields as implemented on the server.

query.name: sort
query.description: (string) Optional. Sort field. Allowed: time, started_at, ended_at, name, tag, location. Other values are ignored for sort selection and default ordering rules apply.

query.name: order
query.description: (string) Optional. Sort direction: asc or desc. Other values are normalized to desc.

query.name: filter
query.description: (string) Optional. Filter string parsed as semicolon-separated segments (for example department=1,2;tag=3,na). Department, division, and location segments use numeric ids; tag supports comma-separated ids or na for untagged. Equivalent array encodings may be merged by the server into that string form.
